children: The work will initially affect about 5 million passengers annually, while carriers have objected to proposed cuts in international departure slots during the transition

Adani Airports will proceed with the phased redevelopment of Mumbai Airport’s Terminal 1 from January 2027, despite airlines opposing a proposed temporary reduction in international departure slots at the airport and resisting a shift of part of their operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport.

Mumbai International Airport or MIAL, operated by Adani Airport Holdings or AAHL, plans to redevelop the North Section of Terminal 1B, citing safety concerns around the 60-year-old infrastructure. The section represents around one-third of Terminal 1’s capacity. Adani Airports said around 5 million passengers annually, or about 9 per cent of Mumbai Airport’s total traffic, will be temporarily deoperationalised during the redevelopment.

The phased redevelopment is intended to allow the airport to continue operations rather than require a complete shutdown of Terminal 1. Adani Airports has offered airlines the option of temporarily relocating operations to Navi Mumbai International Airport, which is also operated by AAHL. The operator has said the transition would be temporary and that Mumbai Airport would regain its historical slots, along with additional slots, after the redevelopment.

However, airlines have opposed a separate proposal to temporarily discontinue 265 of 770 weekly international departure slots at Mumbai Airport from 25 October. The vacated capacity at Terminal 2 would be used to accommodate domestic traffic shifted from Terminal 1 during the redevelopment, according to a media report.

The proposed reduction would affect 46 airlines operating international services from Mumbai. IndiGo faces a proposed reduction of 74 weekly international departure slots from its existing 224, while Air India could see 33 slots reduced from 100. Akasa Air and Air India Express face proposed reductions of 11 and seven weekly international departures, respectively, while Emirates and Etihad Airways could each lose 10 slots, according to media report.

In a 2 October communication to MIAL, the Airline Operators Committee-Mumbai said its members did not accept the proposed reduction, cancellation or withdrawal of established international departure slots. The airlines said their support for the redevelopment of Terminal 1 should not be interpreted as consent to the proposed reduction in international capacity.

The AOC-Mumbai has also sought the technical and operational basis for the proposed 33 per cent reduction, including MIAL’s assessment of airport capacity, planned enhancements at Terminal 2 and the demand-capacity analysis supporting the proposal. The matter has also been escalated to the Directorate General of Civil Aviation, Ministry of Civil Aviation and Airports Economic Regulatory Authority, according report.

Adani Airports has asked carriers to identify by 4 pm on 6 October the international departure slots they want temporarily discontinued. If airlines do not respond, the airport operator has said it will select the slots based on operational, capacity and implementation considerations.

“91 per cent of Mumbai Airport’s passenger traffic will remain unaffected even as we undertake redevelopment of the age-old infrastructure that was in urgent need of repairs. Only the North Section of Terminal 1B, which accounts for around one-third of T1 of Mumbai Airport’s capacity, is being demolished in Phase 1 to minimise passenger inconvenience and operational disruption. The transition to Navi Mumbai Airport is temporary and does not represent a permanent shift of Mumbai Airport traffic,” said Arun Bansal, CEO, Adani Airport Holdings.
Terminal 1 Capacity To Rise 33%

Adani Airports said Terminal 1 has been a safety-related concern for several years, with temporary mitigation measures used in the absence of an alternative for passengers and airlines. The airport operator said the risks associated with continued operations became more pronounced following a fire at the terminal in April. The availability of Navi Mumbai International Airport has enabled the redevelopment to be planned in phases, it said.

The redevelopment is expected to increase Terminal 1’s annual capacity by 33 per cent, from 15 million passengers to 20 million passengers. Adani Airports has also said the redeveloped terminal will restore all historical slots and provide additional slots for airlines.

“Extensive consultations with airlines on the future of Terminal 1 have been ongoing since 2020, and the proposed redevelopment was also presented before AERA and subsequently incorporated into the approved tariff framework. While we appreciate the concerns expressed by certain airlines, passenger safety must remain paramount, and any further delay in commencing this process could adversely impact the safety and convenience of millions of travellers,” Bansal said.

The airline objections come amid wider concerns over the proposed division of operations between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai. According to report that the International Air Transport Association has opposed forced airline relocations, while Air France-KLM has said splitting its passenger operations between the two airports is not an option.
Incentives For Navi Mumbai Operations

Navi Mumbai International Airport is offering a 100 per cent discount on landing fees for new international flights. Adani Airports also plans to provide cash vouchers to international passengers to offset the difference in User Development Fees charged at Navi Mumbai and Mumbai airports.

The operator has argued that the availability of Navi Mumbai provides the capacity needed to redevelop Terminal 1 without shutting down the entire facility. The two airports are both operated by AAHL, which manages eight airports and serves more than 23 per cent of India’s total passenger traffic, according to the company.

“Its availability makes it possible to undertake the redevelopment of T1 of Mumbai Airport in phases, instead of shutting down the entire terminal and causing greater disruption to passengers and airlines,” Bansal said.

The redevelopment is scheduled to begin in January 2027, but the proposed interim changes to international operations remain contested by airlines. The dispute is now centred on how Mumbai’s existing international capacity will be managed while domestic traffic from Terminal 1 is shifted to Terminal 2.
